items.title: 1.2 Modern periodic table: features and significance

source_refs.note: Topic 1.2, printed page 3: the features of the modern periodic table.

blocks.text: The classification of elements in the modern periodic table makes their properties easier to understand. Its main features are these.

items: 118 elements are grouped in ascending order of their atomic numbers.
There are seven horizontal rows, the periods, and eighteen vertical columns, the groups. In older versions of the table the vertical groups were divided into eight A groups and ten B groups.

Elements within the same group exhibit similar chemical properties because they have the same number of valence electrons, but they show a gradual change in physical properties from top to bottom of the group.
Elements in a period show a gradual change in properties moving from left to right.

blocks.text: Besides groups and periods, the elements are grouped into blocks, families and categories to enhance understanding.

blocks.alt: A schematic periodic table of seven period rows and eighteen group columns. The s block is pink at the left, the d block blue in the middle, the p block cream at the right, and the two f block rows purple below; a thick black stair-step line runs from boron down to polonium, and symbols mark the edges of each block. A legend explains the blocks, the line and the families.
blocks.caption: The modern periodic table: periods, groups, blocks, families and the stair-step line (original schematic after Figures 1.1 and 10.2).
blocks.long_description: Seven periods run across and eighteen groups run down. Groups 1 and 2 (with helium) are the s block, groups 13 to 18 the p block, groups 3 to 12 the d block of transition metals, and the lanthanides and actinides below the f block. The stair-step line from boron to polonium separates metals on the left from non-metals on the right, with the metalloids along it. The families are the alkali metals (group 1), alkaline earth metals (group 2), transition metals, chalcogens (group 16), halogens (group 17) and noble gases (group 18).

blocks.prompt: Chlorine and bromine are in the same group; chlorine and argon are in the same period. Which pair has similar chemical properties, and why?
blocks.explanation: Chlorine and bromine, because elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, which decides chemical behaviour; their physical properties change only gradually down the group. Chlorine and argon lie in the same period, where properties change step by step from left to right, so they differ sharply.

items: 118 elements in order of atomic number; 7 periods and 18 groups (older tables: 8 A and 10 B groups).
Same group: same valence electrons, similar chemistry, gradual change in physical properties. Same period: gradual change from left to right. Blocks, families and categories are extra groupings.
